Pozniak et al. conducted a systematic analysis of national HIV treatment cascades to evaluate the feasibility of achieving the UNAIDS 90-90-90 target, as published in BMJ Global Health in 2016. 2. The 2016 UNAIDS Prevention Gap Report highlighted the gaps in HIV prevention efforts globally. 3. The 2019 UNAIDS Global AIDS Update emphasized the importance of placing communities at the center of HIV response strategies. 4. Kalichman et al. systematically reviewed the prevalence of sexually transmitted co-infections in people living with HIV/AIDS and discussed the implications for using HIV treatments as prevention, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2011. 5. Dalal et al. demonstrated that assisted partner notification services improve HIV test uptake and case finding, as reported in AIDS in 2017. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) updated its recommendations on firstand second-line antiretroviral regimens in 2019 to improve treatment outcomes. 7. WHO's 2018 HIV Self-Testing Strategic Framework provided guidance for planning, introducing, and scaling up self-testing initiatives. 8. The International AIDS Society published a decision framework in 2018 for differentiated HIV testing services to optimize delivery. 9. WHO's 2016 guidelines on HIV self-testing and partner notification supplemented its consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services. 10. WHO's 2015 consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services provided comprehensive recommendations for improving testing strategies. 11. WHO's second edition of the 2016 guidelines on antiretroviral therapy emphasized a public health approach to HIV treatment. 12. WHO's 2019 HIV Molecular Diagnostics Toolkit aimed to enhance access to viral load testing and early infant diagnosis. 13. Stover et al. updated the Spectrum model in 2014 to estimate key HIV indicators for adults and children, as published in AIDS. 14. Hart Prieto and Jones compared pediatric surgery outcomes between district general hospitals and regional referral centers, as reported in Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England in 2011. 15. The Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS) 2016-2017 provided a population-based assessment of HIV's impact, with its final report published in 2018. 16. Katz et al. explored the use of HIV partner services and social network approaches to improve testing among key populations, as outlined in WHO's 2019 report. 17. Bassett et al. demonstrated the effectiveness of mobile HIV testing and geospatial mapping in reaching hard-to-reach populations in Umlazi Township, Durban, South Africa, as published in AIDS and Behavior in 2015. 18. Dwyer-Lindgren et al. mapped HIV prevalence trends in sub-Saharan Africa from 2000 to 2017, as published in Nature in 2019. 19. WHO's 2019 consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services emphasized the importance of affordable and accurate testing strategies, including the use of rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) and enzyme immunoassays (EIAs). 20. WHO recommended the use of three consecutive reactive test results for HIV-positive diagnosis in high-burden countries to ensure accuracy as HIV positivity rates decline. 21. WHO discouraged the use of Western blotting and line immunoassays in HIV testing algorithms, advocating for RDTs and EIAs instead. 22. HIV self-testing and triage testing using trained lay providers were recommended to reach individuals unaware of their HIV status. 23. Dual HIV/syphilis RDTs were suggested as the first test for pregnant women in antenatal care, except for those on ART or previously treated for syphilis. 24. WHO emphasized the need for national programs to build and verify HIV testing algorithms and prepare for potential product shortages. 25. Efficient HIV diagnosis enables timely initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART), benefiting individual health and reducing community transmission. 26. Evidence shows that individuals on ART with viral suppression do not transmit HIV to their sexual partners. 27. Effective diagnosis also allows HIV-negative individuals to access prevention interventions such as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC). 28. WHO highlighted the importance of addressing underserved populations, including adolescents, young people, and key populations such as men who have sex with men, people who inject drugs, and sex workers. 29. WHO's updated recommendations encouraged countries to adopt three consecutive reactive test results for HIV diagnosis and to discontinue outdated testing methods. 30. Dual HIV/syphilis RDTs were recommended for antenatal care settings to improve maternal and child health outcomes. 31. WHO emphasized the importance of planning and implementing HIV testing services to reach underserved populations and reduce gaps in care. 32. Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) have proven accuracy and reliability in various settings, including resource-constrained environments. 33. Efficient diagnosis facilitates access to prevention and treatment services, improving health outcomes for individuals and communities. 34. WHO's 2019 guidelines highlighted the declining national HIV testing positivity rates in high-burden countries and the need to optimize testing strategies. 35. Countries with low national HIV testing positivity rates were encouraged to refine their testing strategies to improve efficiency and effectiveness. 36. Focused HIV testing in key populations and priority locations was associated with higher positivity rates, reflecting targeted efforts to address the epidemic. 37. WHO emphasized the importance of using national program data to monitor HIV testing positivity and inform strategic planning.
